Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MAP pulse: acceptance roadmap & gating checklist for ACME POC

Hi Emily / team —

Thanks again for the kickoff last week. Per our mutual action plan (MAP), attaching a condensed acceptance roadmap and the evaluation checklist so we have a single source of truth for PO C acceptance. High-level items below and embedded owners in the attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx, eval-checklist.md (see attachments).

Quick summary:
- POC window: May 10–May 31 (technical validation + QA run)
- Acceptance gate: functional + perf + compliance evidence by May 28
- Decision target (close/expand): June 7 exec review

This week’s pulse / meeting (Wed 5/5 10am PT): focus on two open blockers — procurement timeline + SOC2 evidence request — and finalize the perf acceptance criteria.

Draft acceptance criteria (short):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 200ms for 1k token sequences (see perf notes)
- Throughput: sustained 5 req/s under continuous load (50 concurrent users sim)
- Output quality: sample evals pass accept threshold (AUC >= 0.85 on labeled prompts)
- Data handling: logs retained per agreed retention window, no customer data persisted beyond session as per MAP

Action items I’ve added in the sheet: owners + dates. Please review and flag any missing items before the meeting.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-checklist.md (markdown)

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP pulse: acceptance roadmap & gating checklist for ACME POC

Thanks — adding some technical clarity so acceptance criteria are testable in the POC:

Perf specifics (to include in eval-checklist.md):
- Warm-start 95p latency <= 200ms (measured over five 10-minute windows across test days). Cold-start allowed to spike but must be documented.
- Token billing: investigate KV cache hit-rate > 75% for repeated prompt families (this impacts cost targets).
- Model variant: we'll run intersection tests on quantized 4-bit vs fp16; final acceptance requires quality parity within 2% on the labeled set.
- Failure modes: graceful fallback to smaller model variant if 90s sustained error rate > 1% (MAP downstream SLO)

Blockers I’m tracking:
- Procurement timeline (Emily noted approvals next week) — impacts ability to enable dedicated capacity for final week.
- SOC2 evidence exchange — I’ll attach the SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) and can schedule a technical walkthrough with your security team.

I’ll bring a short runbook to Wed’s call (test harness, scripts, and sample reports). Priyom — please confirm the synthetic load script version we’ll run (v3.1).

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>

Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP pulse: acceptance roadmap & gating checklist for ACME POC

Laura / Rishi —

Appreciate the detailed checklist. A couple quick notes from Acme’s side:

1) Procurement: Our legal and procurement teams are lined up to start review on Mon 5/10, but we’ll need a redline window of 48–72 hrs to hit your POC enablement target. I’m copying procurement to coordinate signatures.

2) SOC2: we need the SOC2 summary + engineer contact for a brief Q&A. Can you provide a link to the evidence package? PDF is fine; we’ll log it in our compliance tracker.

3) Acceptance criteria: Latency target looks fine, but can we add an availability requirement: >= 99.8% over the POC period with documented incidents? That’s important for our internal risk gate.

4) Small ask: can we compress the dedicated-capacity test to 2 days (May 24–25) instead of a full week if procurement signs early? That would reduce cost for both sides while giving us the perf signal we need.

We’re good to run Wed’s call — Emily

Emily Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Cloud
emily.park@acmecloud.com
